crime: When her arm was broken, {WITCH_NAME} told everyone she had fallen off her bicycle. She told just one girl who had really done it, and how.
One morning a note hung open on her cell bars: “Ask her who really broke her arm.” Everyone going up to breakfast could read it. She took it down and said it was nothing.

The girl who knew always went up last. Another morning, {WITCH_NAME} waited in the empty cell corridor and strangled her with both hands. Then she passed her hands over the girl's throat, her own knuckles, and the scuffed floor until no marks remained.

A prisoner returning for a spoon found the body. The girl's face was dark and her eyes speckled red. Beneath the unmarked skin, a broken throat bone shifted at a touch. The violence remained inside, although its fresh surface traces were gone. {WITCH_NAME}, who could erase those traces, had come up long after the others left the corridor.
fields.epitaph: Her hands could erase a mark, but never something she had told another person.
fields.epithet: The Girl for Whom Nothing Happened
execution: A stone basin held the back of her head as she lay bound beneath a dripping pipe. Each drop landed on her forehead and collected in the basin. The water rose around her face. The drops continued after it covered her mouth and nose, until she drowned.

magic.name: the Unhappening
magic.text: She can erase fresh traces by passing her hand over them.
